harmonicFunction: G (I) - Tonic chord establishing the spiritual foundation and resolution
Em (vi) - Relative minor introducing depth, memory, and solemnity
C (IV) - Subdominant chord adding uplifting emotional swell
Am (ii) - Supertonic minor providing gentle tension before the dominant
D (V) - Dominant chord creating natural harmonic pull back to the tonic G

techniques.name: Solo Acoustic Single-Note Intro Riff
techniques.description: Picking the iconic opening melody on the bottom strings (6, 5, and 4) using alternate picking before launching into the full rhythm strum

notes: Low E string: 3rd fret G note (3.6)
Land squarely on the full open G major chord at the conclusion of the melody
sequence: Count in at 74 BPM with steady quarter-note pulse
Play the single-note line cleanly using fingertips right behind the fret wire
Let each note ring with warm acoustic resonance
Drop immediately into steady 4/4 down-up strumming on G
tips: Use a firm pick attack for authoritative volume
Keep your fretting hand relaxed so transitions between frets 0, 2, and 3 are seamless
Do not rush the tempo — the majesty of Redemption Song comes from its dignified, deliberate pacing
details.progression: Single-note G pentatonic melody into G chord

techniques.name: Relaxed Folk-Reggae Acoustic Strum
techniques.description: A gentle, pulsing acoustic strumming pattern combining rooted downstrokes on beat 1 with light offbeat brushes that evoke Marley's reggae roots on a solo steel-string guitar

notes: Light palm muting or feathering on the backbeat
Open chord resonance across G, Em, C, Am, and D
sequence: Emphasize the bass note on beat 1
Brush through the treble strings on beat 2
Add light upstrokes on the '&' beats
Keep your wrist swinging freely like a pendulum
tips: Avoid heavy, aggressive thrashing — Marley's acoustic playing is light, percussive, and nuanced
Anchor your thumb on the top of the neck to lightly mute the low E string when playing C and Am
Sing from the heart while maintaining steady rhythm

sections.name: Intro Solo Acoustic Riff
sections.description: One of the most famous acoustic guitar intros in recorded history: Marley plays the unadorned single-note G pentatonic line alone before strumming the first G chord.
notes: Hit the 3rd fret on string 6 with your middle finger
Play the ascending run through the 5th and 4th strings
Clean descending turnaround resolving into full open G major chord
sections.exerciseLabel: Bob Marley Legendary Single-Note Intro Riff

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Marley accompanies his unforgettable vocal history with open cowboy chords, moving effortlessly from G to Em, C, Am, and D.
notes: Relax into the slow 74 BPM heartbeat pulse
Clean finger placement on Am and D
Keep the rhythm intimate and unhurried

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The universal singalong chorus: 'Won't you help to sing, these songs of freedom...' rising through G, C, and D.
sections.progression: G - C - D - G - C - D - Em - C - D - G
notes: Strum with open, ringing acoustic resonance
Notice the emotional minor turn when dipping into Em
sections.exerciseLabel: Songs of Freedom Universal Campfire Chorus

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: G major pentatonic scale run across strings 6, 5, and 4 mirroring the exact note choices of the intro riff.
notes: Alternate picking with strict down-up motion
Connect scale positions directly with the G open chord shape
Focus on consistent note duration and tone
sections.exerciseLabel: G Major Pentatonic Intro Scale Study

beginner.title: Master the Single-Note Intro Riff
steps: Learn the note sequence on strings 6, 5, and 4 at 60 BPM
Practice alternate picking (down on string 6, up on string 5)
Work on resolving the riff cleanly into the open G chord
Bring the intro up to the 74 BPM recording tempo

intermediate.title: Learn the Verse & Chorus Progressions
steps: Master the verse chord changes (G - Em - C - Am - D)
Learn the chorus sequence including the Em emotional turn
Develop the relaxed, pulsing acoustic strumming feel
Play through the entire song from intro to outro without stopping

advanced.title: Solo Campfire Performance & Vocals
steps: Sing lead vocals while maintaining the relaxed 74 BPM acoustic groove
Incorporate subtle hammer-on embellishments on the C and Am chords
Deliver the prophetic lyrical narrative with deep emotional resonance
Lead an uplifting campfire group singalong

commonMistakes: Rushing the single-note intro — Marley's delivery is slow, majestic, and grounded at 74 BPM
Hitting wrong strings during the intro run — keep your fretting hand fingers anchored close to the strings
Strumming too aggressively — this is an intimate, solemn acoustic prayer, not a loud rock song
Muting adjacent strings on the Am and D chords
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Open chord finger warm-up across G, Em, C, Am, and D
5 minutes: Isolated drill of the single-note intro riff with a metronome at 70 BPM
5 minutes: Verse chord transitions with steady down-up strumming
5 minutes: Chorus flow and practicing the transition from D into Em
5 minutes: Full run-through singing along with the acoustic guitar
focusAreas: Clean single-note picking on the bottom strings
metronomeWork: Start at 60 BPM to practice the intro riff with steady timing
Increase to 74 BPM once the melody is second nature
Practice setting clicks on beats 2 and 4 to develop natural reggae-folk pocket
Verify you maintain steady tempo between the intro riff and the strumming verse
